title: Unified transport policies + latency-aware pool scaling and cross-SDK examples
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation:
Many SDK consumers are confused by differing transport defaults across Python/TypeScript/Go: per-request deadlines, connection reuse behavior, and streaming reconnect semantics. This causes production incidents (silent stalls, token-cost spikes due to excessive retries, or long tail latency) and makes our docs examples brittle across languages.

Goal:
Provide a single, opinionated set of "transport policy profiles" with clear language idioms and copy-paste examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Profiles should be: conservative (low retry, short deadlines for interactive flows), default (balanced latency/cost), and durable (higher retries, long deadlines for background batch jobs). Additionally introduce an adaptive connection-pool scaler driven by p50/p95 latency windows so dedicated deployments maintain latency SLOs while minimizing idle connections.

Scope / Deliverables:
- SDK API surface: new TransportProfile enum + per-client/ per-route override.
- Cross-language reference implementations (Python, TS, Go) and copyable snippets for docs.
- Adaptive pool scaler: server-side hint interface (X-Conn-Usage hint header / telemetry hooks) and client backpressure guidance.
- Streaming ergonomics: resume token extension, transparent short reconnect + stream-resume for partial outputs, and example retry contract for idempotent vs non-idempotent streaming methods.
- Explicit guidance for TLS session reuse, TCP keepalive tuning, and socket-level timeout recommendations for common clouds.
- Telemetry: new metrics (conn_active, conn_idle_count, conn_acquire_latency_ms, pool_scale_event) and dashboards.

Design decisions summary:
- Default profile will favor lower retries and 3s per-request soft deadline for interactive completions, with an immediate circuit-breaker on streaming stalls > 10s. This reduces amplification in bursty workloads.
- Durable profile increases deadline to 60s and allows exponential backoff up to 3 retries for transient 5xx/network errors.
- Adaptive pool scaler uses a sliding 2-minute window; scale-up when conn_acquire_p95 > 50ms for two consecutive windows; scale-down when p95 < 20ms and idle_ratio > 0.6 for three windows. These heuristics are conservative to avoid flapping.
- Streaming resume: each streaming response may include an optional resume_token. On transient network failure, SDK will attempt up to 2 reconnects within 5s to resume the stream. Resume is only allowed for server-declared resumable endpoints to avoid semantics mismatch.

Cross-SDK examples (copyable):
- Python (requests/asyncio friendly):
  from redwood_sdk import Client, TransportProfile
  client = Client(transport_profile=TransportProfile.DEFAULT, pool_options={"max_idle": 8, "min_idle": 2})
  # per-route override
  client.routes.create("chat", timeout_ms=3000, retries=0)

- TypeScript (node fetch + HTTP/2):
  import { RedwoodClient, TransportProfile } from '@redwood/sdk';
  const c = new RedwoodClient({ transportProfile: TransportProfile.Default, pool: { maxIdle: 12 } });
  // route specific
  c.route('generate').set({ timeoutMs: 3000, retries: 0 });

- Go (net/http + native http2):
  client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithTransportProfile(redwood.TransportProfileDefault), redwood.WithPoolOptions(redwood.PoolOptions{MaxIdle: 10}))
  // per-request context with deadline
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)

Operational notes:
- Recommended OS-level knobs for our hosted infra: tcp_keepalive_time=120, tcp_keepalive_intvl=10, tcp_keepalive_probes=9 to avoid premature tear-downs in noisy cloud networks. For dedicated/private on-prem we suggest shorter timeouts (30s) when inside low-latency LAN.
- TLS session reuse: SDKs should enable session ticket reuse and prefer TLS1.3; surface an option to pin TLS session caches for long-running processes.
- For streaming heavy workloads, enable aggressive prefix caching and prefer HTTP/2 or multiplexed transports to reduce conn churn.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement new TransportProfile enum in all SDKs + default mapping and unit tests.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): add adaptive pool scaler prototype and telemetry hooks; implement server-side hint header.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): streaming resume implementation and docs. Canary across 10% of hosted traffic for 1 week, track conn_acquire_p95, error_rate_stream_resume, and bytes_sent_per_token.

Migration guidance for customers:
- Provide a compatibility shim: legacy clients without TransportProfile continue to use current defaults for 90 days after launch. Warn via SDK logs and console when legacy profile is detected.
